frequencyResponse.pointsContext: The manufacturer EDS table is labeled Frequency Response, Half Space (SPL), with points from 20 to 20,000 Hz. The table does not state an input/reference level, so these values are retained as the published SPL shape only and are not labeled 1 W/1 m. The separately published sensitivity is 100 dB at 1 W/1 m; the simulator may normalize the curve independently. Only listed points are stored, with no interpolation.

notes: Exact-model Electro-Voice Force i engineering data sheet (Part 38110-080 Rev C). Describes a passive 15-inch two-way system with a 15-inch woofer and DH3 1-inch titanium compression driver. Published response limits are 40 Hz–20 kHz at -10 dB and 60 Hz–20 kHz at -3 dB; the stored bounds use the -10 dB range. Sensitivity is explicitly 100 dB at 1 W/1 m. Continuous handling is 250 W (500 W program, 1,000 W short-term are not substituted for continuous handling); nominal impedance is 8 ohms. Manufacturer's half-space response table is imported at its printed points with its incomplete input-reference context preserved. The EDS also publishes coverage and directivity tables; no directivity values are imported because the current SpeakerSpec has no directivity field. Unsupported Fs and voice-coil diameter remain N/A. Source: https://products.electrovoice.com/binary/Force_i_E_EDS.pdf.

Exact-model Electro-Voice Sentry 500 data sheet (manufacturer-authored 1991 document; fetched copy hosted by Manualzz). It describes a passive two-way monitor with a 12-inch woofer and Super-Dome tweeter. Sensitivity is 96 dB at 1 W/1 m, averaged over 300–2,000 Hz in an anechoic environment. Continuous/long-term handling is 100 W at 8 ohms (400 W is the separate 10 ms short-term capacity); nominal impedance is 8 ohms and minimum is 6 ohms. The fetched text gives 40–18,000 Hz but renders its response tolerance as '+3 dB', not an unambiguous ±3 dB; frequency-response bounds therefore remain N/A rather than assuming a tolerance. No response points or polar/directivity data are digitized. Source: https://manualzz.com/doc/22701574/electro-voice-sentry500-data-sheet.

Exact Sx300PI non-transformer record, sourced to the Electro-Voice Sx300PI/Sx300PIX engineering data sheet. The PI system is a passive two-way weather-resistant loudspeaker with a 12-inch DL12Sx woofer and DH2010A high-frequency driver. The manufacturer's A&E specification states 80–25,000 Hz at -3 dB; sensitivity is 99 dB SPL at 1 W/1 m using band-limited pink noise averaged from 300–2,000 Hz; long-term handling is 300 W (1,200 W short-term) for the non-transformer PI; nominal impedance is 8 ohms (6 ohms minimum). Only the explicit response limits are stored: the EDS's plotted responses are not digitized, and its directivity data are not added because the current SpeakerSpec has no directivity field. PIX transformer taps and specifications remain separate and are not transferred to this PI record. Source: https://products.electrovoice.com/binary/Sx300PI_PIX_EDS.pdf.

Exact Sx300PIX record, separately identified by the Electro-Voice Sx300PI/Sx300PIX engineering data sheet as the Sx300PI system fitted with an AT100 transformer. The exact-model documentation supports the shared two-way transducer layout and 12-inch low-frequency driver, so only driverCount=2, passive status, and woofer diameter are populated. The PIX is a constant-voltage transformer model with selectable 70.7 V and 100 V taps (50/70/100 W and 100/140/200 W respectively); its impedance is tap-dependent (50 ohms nominal at the highest tap, 111 ohms at 1 kHz), so no single impedance or scalar power-handling value is asserted. PI sensitivity and response limits/plots are not transferred to PIX. No response points or directivity data are imported. Source: https://products.electrovoice.com/binary/Sx300PI_PIX_EDS.pdf.

Exact Sx100+ family specifications from Electro-Voice-authored manual 535581 Rev E (July 2006; fetched copy hosted by Manualzz). The manual lists Sx100+E and Sx100+WE finish variants; their shared published system specifications support the dataset's Sx100+ family record. Passive two-way system with a 12-inch low-frequency driver; 60 Hz–25 kHz response at -10 dB; 200 W continuous handling (800 W peak is not substituted); nominal impedance 8 ohms (5.6 ohms minimum). The manual lists sensitivity as 98 dB but gives no measurement reference in the fetched document, so referenced sensitivity remains N/A. No response or directivity graph points are digitized; unsupported Fs and voice-coil diameter remain N/A. Source: https://manualzz.com/doc/3125205/electro-voice-sx100--user-s-manual. Both fetched Manualzz URLs (`https://manualzz.com/doc/3125205/electro-voice-sx100--user-s-manual` and `https://manualzz.com/doc/3125205/electrovoice-sx100--user-s-manual`) return the same document 3125205, containing the July 2006, Part Number 535581 Rev E Sx100+ manual; the stored field source uses the hyphenated URL.

Exact Sx300E variant supported by the Electro-Voice Sx300 engineering data sheet, whose part-number list identifies Sx300E (11053031, black) and the separate Sx300WE (11053029, white). The specification block describes the passive 12-inch two-way system with DL12-BFH woofer and 1-inch-exit DH2010A driver. It specifies 50 Hz–20 kHz at -10 dB (60 Hz–20 kHz at -3 dB), sensitivity 99 dB SPL at 1 W/1 m, 300 W continuous/1,200 W peak, and 8 ohms nominal (5 ohms minimum). Only the explicit response limits are stored; no points are imported from the extracted multi-column response/impedance table, and no directivity data are added because the current SpeakerSpec has no directivity field. This Sx300E remains distinct from the dataset's separate unsuffixed Sx300 record. Unsupported Fs and voice-coil diameter remain N/A. Source: https://products.electrovoice.com/binary/Sx300_Engineering_Data_Sheet.pdf.

frequencyResponse.pointsContext: The manufacturer EDS labels this numeric table Frequency Response, Half Space (SPL, 1W/1m, dB), with a footnote identifying a half-space measurement. The listed 20–800 Hz samples are transcribed as printed, without interpolation. The scalar response bounds are separately published as 43–200 Hz (-10 dB); the simulator may normalize the table independently from the scalar sensitivity.

notes: Exact Electro-Voice SB122 engineering data sheet (the document body identifies SB122 despite different PDF metadata). Passive one-driver subwoofer using an EVS12SB 12-inch driver. Published response limits are 52–145 Hz at -3 dB and 43–200 Hz at -10 dB; stored bounds use the -10 dB range. Sensitivity is 99 dB SPL at 1 W/1 m, half-space; power handling is 400 W continuous and 1,600 W peak; nominal impedance is 8 ohms. The EDS's half-space SPL/1 W/1 m response samples from 20 to 800 Hz are imported exactly as printed; no interpolation or graph digitization. No unsupported Fs or voice-coil diameter is inferred. Source: https://products.electrovoice.com/binary/SB122%20EDS.pdf.
